A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MARS-Sep and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original separation results on VGGSOUND-clean+ and MUSIC-clean+, encoder and training ablations, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, sensitivity and fusion experiments, efficiency measurements, and a human listening study.

M1.justification: The Beta mask policy, clipped optimization objective, multimodal pooled reward, and three-stage encoder alignment remain unchanged. The preference-alignment terminology reorganizes existing components; alternative fusion mechanisms are evaluated as ablations, without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate VGGSOUND-clean+ and MUSIC-clean+ under text, audio, image, and composed queries. The listening study samples existing test data. Newly emphasized in-the-wild coverage is not accompanied by identifiable additional data or changed qualitative examples in the PDFs.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add LASS-Net for text queries, iQuery for image queries, and DAVIS-Flow for both. New Table 3 evaluates FlowSep and ZeroSep against MARS-Sep using CLAP metrics. The original comparators remain, substantially broadening the evaluated competition.

E3.justification: v2 adds audio-to-audio CLAP scoring, hyperparameter sweeps, efficiency benchmarking, and a randomized listening protocol with 100 query-audio pairs, 10 listeners, Likert ratings, and preferences against target audio. Original benchmark settings largely persist. Tables 6–7 introduce entropy/KL defaults of 0.2/0.1, conflicting with 0.1/0.01 in unchanged Appendix D; this does not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.1.1 tests sensitivity to concentration, clipping, entropy, and KL parameters. E.1.2 compares MLBP with maximum pooling, average pooling, and learned weighted sums on both benchmarks. Efficiency profiling and human semantic-alignment validation supplement the retained encoder ablations and case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report means with dispersion and retain Appendix C's description of standard deviations or 95% bootstrap intervals. v2 adds no training-run counts, seeds, or significance tests. Additional uncertainty values accompany new results without establishing a changed statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial baseline, sensitivity, fusion, efficiency, and listener results. Table 2 changes MARS-Sep's MUSIC text-query CLAP score from 5.18±0.01 to 6.18±0.93 without explaining the revision; other matched original results remain unchanged. New Table 15 reports semantic ratings of 3.57±0.48 for MARS-Sep versus 3.42±0.51 for OmniSep.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14, the MDP formulation, policy objective, alignment losses, pooling definition, and SI-SDR derivation are retained. The preference-alignment framing adds conceptual explanation, without new formal assumptions, proofs, or mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly present separation as human-preference alignment and meta-reasoning analogous to LLM alignment. The contribution list explicitly extends its empirical claim to synthesized and in-the-wild samples. The principal algorithmic contributions and conclusion remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of hyperparameter sensitivity, fusion behavior, generative CLAP variability, human agreement, and training-versus-inference cost. Appendix E.3 softens the earlier image-query qualification despite unchanged results. Some new interpretations exceed the evidence: E.1.2 claims a weighted-sum advantage for audio queries that Table 8 does not show.

D1.justification: The anonymous code pointer is replaced by a GitHub repository pointer. Appendix E.4 adds A800 hardware, memory, training-time, and inference-batch information. The original implementation and training appendices remain substantially unchanged; repository accessibility cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Related work gains a focused discussion of generative separation, including FlowSep, DAVIS, and DAVIS-Flow, and expands discussion of already-cited ZeroSep. Speech/dialogue citations are added, while Factually Augmented RLHF and RLHF-V are removed. The broader separation and RLHF positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, expands the introductory motivation and method overview, condenses the RLHF review, and adds experimental subsections. Equal-contribution notation, conference headers, and acknowledgments are added. The main section sequence and most technical prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded main comparison tables and new displays for generative CLAP results, sensitivity, fusion, efficiency, and human evaluation substantially enlarge the quantitative presentation. Figures 1–4 remain unchanged, and earlier appendix tables are retained with new numbering. New Table 14 reverses the hardware and memory column headings relative to their contents.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the evidence through broader comparisons, component controls, and human evaluation addressing the central semantic-alignment claim. Efficiency reporting also exposes approximately doubled training time. These benefits are limited by conflicting hyperparameter defaults, inaccurate interpretation of the fusion results, and insufficient support for attributing competitors' higher CLAP scores to inflation. The additions provide a net improvement, but their reporting inconsistencies prevent a clear substantial overall quality gain.
